structure:
A single short Markdown ruling file, 71 lines (workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-ian-2026-11-16.md), from Ian, dated 16 November 2026, on whether the consignor party picker must also list addresses saved for an exporter role. It has four sections: a title paragraph that names the question and quotes the judge's challenge raised while reviewing inc-087 in the consignment-parties theme; "What was asked", which quotes inc-087's acceptance criterion 2 verbatim with its three citations and then sets out the code evidence that no exporter role exists (the address book's six-role vocabulary, an empty grep for EXPORTER, holdsRole taking a single role, each party binding exactly one addressBookRole); "Decided", five numbered points; and "What this changes in the backlog", four bullets. Scope is the whole file and nothing is left out. At 71 lines with every word load-bearing it is well inside one agent's reading, so it is one part.

Extracted in 1 part:
Part 1, Whole ruling: Part 1, "Whole ruling": the whole of workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-ian-2026-11-16.md, all 71 lines, read in full. The file is Ian's ruling of 16 November 2026 on whether the consignor party picker must also list addresses saved for an exporter role. Four sections, all covered here: (a) the title paragraph naming the question and block-quoting the judge's challenge raised while ruling on inc-087's review in the consignment-parties theme (lines 1-6); (b) "What was asked" (lines 8-24), which block-quotes inc-087 acceptance criterion 2 verbatim with its three citations, then sets out the code evidence that no exporter role exists — the address book's six-role vocabulary, an empty grep for EXPORTER over the address-book Java source, holdsRole taking a single role, and each party binding exactly one addressBookRole; (c) "Decided" (lines 26-61), five numbered points: the clause is dropped, it was an identifiable distillation error in two prototype claims, the third citation is the rule that refuses it, what the prototype actually says is already built, and adding an EXPORTER role would be the wrong fix; (d) "What this changes in the backlog" (lines 63-71), four bullets: inc-087's open question cleared and the row left done, no requirement changing state and nothing adopted, the address-book theme handed nothing and a future re-distil refused, and the general point that ruling:ian-2026-11-11 point 2's bar on app/data/*.js is on what the file is rather than on how a claim is labelled. There is no other part. Claims are recorded in the order the file makes them; three gaps record what the file touches but leaves open (whether the criterion's text is amended, whether anything else rests on the same two prototype claims, and whether app/routes.js is formally barred as app/data/*.js is).

claims.statement: The ruling settles one question: whether the consignor party picker must also list addresses saved for an exporter role. The question was raised by the judge while ruling on inc-087's review in the consignment-parties theme.
claims.quote: On whether the consignor party picker must also list addresses saved for an **exporter** role, raised by the judge while ruling on `inc-087`'s review in the `consignment-parties` theme:
claims.note: Scope statement for the whole ruling; the decision itself is claim ruling-ian-2026-11-16-p1-011.

claims.statement: The judge's challenge asked where inc-087's acceptance criterion came from, V4 or the prototype, and flagged that the role may not exist at all.
claims.quote: Where did that acceptance criteria come from? The v4 or the prototype? If the role doesn't exist...
claims.note: This is the question put, not a decision. The ruling answers its provenance half at points 2 and 3 and its existence half at point 1. The quote trails off in the source as written.

claims.statement: inc-087's acceptance criterion 2, as written, says the consignor picker lists the organisation's addresses saved for the consignor role together with those saved for the exporter role.
claims.quote: The consignor picker lists the organisation's addresses saved for the consignor role together with those saved for the exporter role, and the roles and addresses page's party sections are Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer and Place of destination
claims.note: Recorded as what the criterion asked, not as a surviving requirement: the exporter half of this clause is dropped by point 1 (claim ruling-ian-2026-11-16-p1-011).

claims.statement: The second half of inc-087's acceptance criterion 2 says the roles and addresses page's party sections are Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer and Place of destination.
claims.quote: the roles and addresses page's party sections are Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer and Place of destination
claims.note: Five sections, no exporter among them. Point 4 keeps this half and says inc-087 satisfies it.

claims.statement: inc-087's acceptance criterion 2 cites three claims on the same line: prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-064 and prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-137 from prototype:dr2-1-source, and ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116 from ruling:sam-2026-10-09.
claims.ref: ruling-ian-2026-11-16.md "What was asked", quoted criterion citations (lines 15-16)
claims.quote: (`prototype:dr2-1-source` prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-064, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-137; `ruling:sam-2026-10-09` ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116)

claims.statement: No code in the inc-087 row could satisfy the exporter clause of criterion 2.
claims.quote: No code in the row could satisfy the exporter clause.

claims.statement: The address book's whole role vocabulary is six roles: PLACE_OF_ORIGIN, CONSIGNOR, PLACE_OF_DESTINATION, CONSIGNEE, IMPORTER and BRANCH_ADDRESS.
claims.quote: The address book's whole role vocabulary is `PLACE_OF_ORIGIN`, `CONSIGNOR`, `PLACE_OF_DESTINATION`, `CONSIGNEE`, `IMPORTER` and `BRANCH_ADDRESS` (`tests:domain/shared/constants/address-types.ts:20-27`)
claims.note: No exporter role in the vocabulary.

claims.statement: A recursive search for EXPORTER across the address book service's Java source returns nothing, so the address book service holds no exporter role.
claims.quote: `grep -rn "EXPORTER"` over `repos/trade-imports-address-book/src/main/java/` returns nothing

claims.statement: Neither frontend can ask the address book for two roles at once: holdsRole takes a single role.
claims.quote: neither frontend can ask for two roles: `holdsRole` takes a single role (`frontend:src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:22-23`)

claims.statement: Each party on the roles and addresses page binds exactly one addressBookRole.
claims.quote: each party binds exactly one `addressBookRole` (`frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/parties.js:13-50`)

claims.statement: The exporter clause of inc-087's acceptance criterion 2 is dropped.
claims.quote: **The exporter clause of `inc-087`'s criterion 2 is dropped.**
claims.note: Answers the question the ruling opens with (claim ruling-ian-2026-11-16-p1-001) and the judge's challenge (claim ruling-ian-2026-11-16-p1-002).

claims.statement: Dropping the exporter clause is final: it is not deferred and not handed to another theme.
claims.quote: It is not deferred, not handed to another theme, and not a reason to add a role.

claims.statement: There is no exporter role and there never was one, and none is to be created to satisfy the dropped clause.
claims.quote: There is no exporter role, there never was one, and none is to be created for this.

claims.statement: The exporter clause was a distillation error, and the error is identifiable.
claims.quote: **It was a distillation error, and the error is identifiable.**

claims.statement: Both prototype claims behind the exporter clause record the prototype's own internal type vocabulary, not a domain role.
claims.quote: Both prototype claims behind the clause are the prototype's own internal type vocabulary, not a domain role:

claims.statement: The first claim behind the clause, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-064, is verbatim from the prototype's app/routes.js lines 3851-3876 and quotes the literal line 'consignor-or-exporter': ['consignor-or-exporter', 'consignor', 'exporter'].
claims.quote: `prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-064` (verbatim, `app/routes.js:3851-3876`) quotes the literal line `'consignor-or-exporter': ['consignor-or-exporter', 'consignor', 'exporter']`.

claims.statement: The second claim behind the clause, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-137, is inferred from the prototype's app/data/consignment-address-sections.js lines 15-28, quotes id: 'consignor-or-exporter', heading: 'Consignor', and read it as the consignor section covering the exporter too with no separate exporter section and the page naming only the consignor.
claims.quote: `prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-137` (inferred, `app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:15-28`) quotes `id: 'consignor-or-exporter', heading: 'Consignor'` and reads it as "the consignor section covers the exporter too: there is no separate exporter section, and the page names only the consignor".

claims.statement: The second claim is taken from app/data/*.js, which ruling:ian-2026-11-11 point 2 already bars a row from resting on, because those files are demo fixtures and a claim from them is evidence of nothing except what the prototype happened to hard-code.
claims.quote: The second of those is a claim taken from `app/data/*.js`, which `ruling:ian-2026-11-11` point 2 already bars a row from resting on: those files are demo fixtures, and a `data` claim from them "is evidence of nothing except what the prototype happened to hard-code".

claims.statement: The first claim comes from app/routes.js, the prototype's own routing glue, which is the same kind of source as app/data/*.js one level further in and so is no better a basis for a domain role.
claims.quote: The first is `app/routes.js`, the prototype's own routing glue — the same thing one level further in.

claims.statement: The third citation on the criterion's same line is the one that refuses the exporter clause.
claims.quote: **The third citation on the same line is the one that refuses the clause.**

claims.statement: ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116 quotes Sam saying the prototype is the authority for how things look and feel, not for how they are architected.
claims.quote: `ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116` quotes Sam directly: *"Prototype is the authority for how things look and feel not how they are architected"*

claims.statement: The statement of ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116 is that the address record's field shape for address uses and roles is the address book service's design.
claims.quote: its statement is that "the address record's field shape for address uses and roles is the address book service's design"

claims.statement: A role vocabulary is architecture, so it is not something the prototype has authority over.
claims.quote: A role vocabulary is architecture.
claims.note: The second half of the statement follows from claim ruling-ian-2026-11-16-p1-021: the prototype's authority stops at look and feel.

claims.statement: inc-087's criterion 2 cited the rule that forbids the exporter clause beside the two claims that broke it.
claims.quote: The criterion cited the rule that forbids it, beside the claims that broke it.

claims.statement: What the prototype actually says is already built.
claims.quote: **What the prototype actually says is already built.**

claims.statement: The prototype's consignor-or-exporter identifier expresses that one section covers both parties, with no separate exporter section.
claims.quote: `consignor-or-exporter` is the prototype's way of expressing that **one section covers both parties** — there is no separate exporter section

claims.statement: The heading of that single section reads "Consignor".
claims.quote: the heading reads "Consignor"

claims.statement: One section covering both parties under the Consignor heading is look and feel, and so is within the prototype's authority.
claims.quote: That is look and feel, it is within the prototype's authority

claims.statement: The real service already models the merged consignor-and-exporter party as the single CONSIGNOR role.
claims.quote: the real service already models it as the single `CONSIGNOR` role

claims.statement: The second half of criterion 2 states the merged party plainly: five party sections, Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer and Place of destination, with no exporter among them.
claims.quote: The second half of the same criterion states it plainly: five party sections, Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer and Place of destination, no exporter among them.
claims.note: The kept half of the criterion quoted at claim ruling-ian-2026-11-16-p1-004, now read as the decided specification.

claims.statement: inc-087 satisfies the five-party-sections half of criterion 2, so the row is correct as built and needs no further work.
claims.quote: `inc-087` satisfies that half, so the row is correct as built and needs no further work.

claims.statement: Adding an EXPORTER role would be the wrong fix.
claims.quote: **Adding an `EXPORTER` role would be the wrong fix.**

claims.statement: Adding an EXPORTER role would split a party the design deliberately merged.
claims.quote: It would split a party the design deliberately merged

claims.statement: Adding an EXPORTER role would put work on the address-book theme that no requirement asks for.
claims.quote: it would put work on the `address-book` theme that no requirement asks for

claims.statement: No row in any theme is to add an EXPORTER role.
claims.quote: No row in any theme is to add one.

claims.statement: inc-087's open question is answered and cleared.
claims.ref: ruling-ian-2026-11-16.md "What this changes in the backlog", first bullet (line 65)
claims.quote: `inc-087`'s open question is answered and cleared.

claims.ref: ruling-ian-2026-11-16.md "What this changes in the backlog", first bullet (line 65)
claims.quote: The row stays `done`; nothing is rebuilt.

claims.statement: No requirement changes state because of this ruling.
claims.ref: ruling-ian-2026-11-16.md "What this changes in the backlog", second bullet (line 66)
claims.quote: No requirement changes state.

claims.quote: This ruling adopts nothing new — it removes a clause that no source supported.

claims.quote: The `address-book` theme is not handed anything.

claims.quote: Should a future re-distil re-draft the exporter clause from the same two prototype claims, this ruling refuses it.

claims.statement: ruling:ian-2026-11-11 point 2 bars app/data/*.js as a source of data, and this case shows the same files being read for a rule, labelled kind: rule rather than kind: data, and still reaching an acceptance criterion.
claims.ref: ruling-ian-2026-11-16.md "What this changes in the backlog", fourth bullet (lines 69-71)
claims.quote: A general point worth carrying: `ruling:ian-2026-11-11` point 2 bars `app/data/*.js` as a source of **data**. This case shows the same files being read for a **rule** (`kind: rule`, not `kind: data`) and reaching a criterion anyway.

claims.statement: The bar on the prototype's app/data files applies to what the file is, not to how a claim taken from it is labelled, so a rule claim from those files is refused as readily as a data one.
claims.ref: ruling-ian-2026-11-16.md "What this changes in the backlog", fourth bullet (line 71)
claims.quote: The bar is on what the file is, not on how the claim is labelled.

claims.statement: The ruling leaves open whether inc-087's acceptance criterion 2 text is edited in the backlog to delete the exporter clause, or left as written with this ruling standing over it: it says the clause is dropped and that no requirement changes state, but never says which.
claims.ref: ruling-ian-2026-11-16.md "Decided" point 1 (line 28) read with "What this changes in the backlog", second bullet (line 66)
claims.note: Point 1 drops the clause and the backlog section says the row stays done and no requirement changes state; whether the stored criterion wording is amended is not said.

claims.statement: The ruling leaves open whether anything other than inc-087's criterion 2 rests on prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-064 or prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-137, and whether those two claims should be withdrawn or re-stated in the extract itself rather than only refused where they reached this criterion.

claims.note: The ruling refuses a future re-draft of the exporter clause from those claims, but says nothing about the claims' own standing or other uses of them.

claims.statement: The ruling leaves open whether the prototype's app/routes.js is formally barred as a source the way app/data/*.js is: it calls routes.js the same thing one level further in, but the general point it carries names only app/data/*.js.
claims.ref: ruling-ian-2026-11-16.md "Decided" point 2, closing paragraph (lines 43-44) read with "What this changes in the backlog", fourth bullet (lines 69-71)
